taxonomy.note: Kew recognizes var. ashei and var. marilandica; B011 remains species-level.

evidence: Kew/POWO accepts Q. marilandica, lists Texas as native, and recognizes var. ashei and var. marilandica.
USDA PLANTS-derived county/native-status data records Q. marilandica as native in Bell County.
The same USDA-derived data records it as native in Blanco County.
The same USDA-derived data records it as native in Burnet County.
target_zone_range.guardrail: The learner remains species-level for B011 while preserving Kew's accepted infraspecific structure; flower/leaf variation should not be used to assign a variety without stronger evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Look for the 'duck-foot' or spatula-shaped leaf and the bark together: the leaf narrows toward the base and ends in 3–5 broad bristle-tipped lobes, while mature bark becomes very dark and blocky.
diagnostic_traits: deciduous red-oak-group tree, often small to medium sized on poor uplands
leaf strongly obovate/obtrullate, narrow below and broad toward tip
usually 3–5 broad shallow lobes concentrated in distal half
upper surface dark glossy green; lower surface paler and often tawny-pubescent
mature bark nearly black to dark gray, breaking into thick squarish blocks

confusers.separator: Post oak is a white-oak-group species with rounded, non-bristle lobes and often a cruciform leaf; blackjack has bristle-tipped lobes and very dark blocky bark.
Water oak can develop spatulate three-lobed leaves but usually has smaller, thinner leaves and lacks blackjack's thick leathery 'duck-foot' form and blocky black bark.
Texas red oak has deeper pointed sinuses and more classically red-oak lobed leaves; blackjack is broader and more top-heavy with shallow distal lobes.

installation_guardrail: Do not install until Calvin explicitly approves B011 pass taxa.
